summary: Feed s114_double to IDS is degraded: 28.9% of frames are sliced to ~256 bytes and 58.0% remain ERSPAN-encapsulated, both preventing full payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker has slicing/snap-length set to ~256 bytes, likely to save bandwidth or fit the 1Gbps tool port, cutting payload before delivery.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature matching; 513/1773 truncated frames hide application data causing missed exploits and high false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing and forward full 1518B frames so IDS receives complete payload for detection; use filtering instead of slicing if bandwidth is constrained.

findings.root_cause: Traffic is forwarded via ERSPAN tunnel from remote source (1029 frames) and broker forwards outer encapsulation without stripping.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees outer ERSPAN/GRE headers instead of inner IP/TCP payload for 58% of traffic and cannot parse or apply signatures, effectively blind to tunneled flows.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to strip ERSPAN encapsulation and present inner original packets so IDS can inspect normally.
